title: HTTP API
summary: This file serves the pipeline over HTTP with FastAPI. `POST /ask` takes a question and returns the full `Answer` as JSON; `POST /ingest` lets an administrator upload PDF, TXT or Markdown files into the index; `GET /health` reports the chunk count and generator. Because `/ingest` changes what every user is answered from, it is off unless an admin key is configured, and uploads are capped in count, size and PDF pages.

key_ideas.explain: In RAG, whoever can add documents controls the answers everyone gets. An open ingest endpoint would let anyone plant false policies or prompt-injection text. Requiring an admin key turns that into a deliberate, authorised action.

Files are read in 1 MB pieces and rejected as soon as they pass the size cap, so a huge upload never fully enters memory. File count and PDF page count are capped too, since text extraction and embedding cost grows with pages.

`secrets.compare_digest` takes the same time whether the first or the last character differs. A normal `==` can stop at the first mismatch, and an attacker timing many requests could learn the key character by character.
The pipeline (and its models) is created on the first request, not when the module is imported. Tests can pass their own lightweight pipeline, and importing `rag.api` stays fast.
The request body is declared as a Pydantic model with limits (question 1 to 1000 characters, `k` 1 to 20). FastAPI rejects bad input with HTTP 422 before your code runs.

blocks.note: Module docstring: how to run the server (`uvicorn rag.api:app --port 8000`), the three endpoints, how the sample corpus is indexed at start-up from `RAG_CORPUS_DIR` (an empty string means start empty), and the security rules for `/ingest`: off unless `RAG_ADMIN_KEY` is set, then the key is required in `X-API-Key`, and uploads are capped by the three `RAG_MAX_*` settings.
`from __future__ import annotations` makes every type hint a lazy string. You can then write `list[str]` or `str | None` on older Pythons (3.8, 3.9) and name a class inside its own body.

Imports the `ingest` module itself under the name `limits`, instead of importing the constants. The code then reads `limits.MAX_FILE_BYTES` at request time, so a test can change `rag.ingest.MAX_FILE_BYTES` (monkeypatch) and the API sees the new value. `from .ingest import MAX_FILE_BYTES` would copy the value once at import and never see the change.

`_check_admin` guards `/ingest`. It returns nothing on success and raises an HTTP error otherwise.
Reads the admin key from the environment at request time. An empty string means no key is configured.
With no key configured, ingestion is disabled entirely: HTTP 403 Forbidden with a message saying how to enable it. Safe by default.

L43: rejects a missing key, or a wrong one. `secrets.compare_digest` compares the two byte strings in constant time, which resists timing attacks. `.encode()` turns both into bytes, which `compare_digest` accepts even for non-ASCII keys.
L44: HTTP 403 with a generic message that does not reveal whether the key was missing or wrong in which way.

`_read_capped` is an `async` function: reading an upload is I/O, so it awaits instead of blocking the server. The docstring states the idea: read in chunks and stop as soon as the cap is passed.
A growable byte buffer.

`while chunk := await f.read(_READ_CHUNK):` uses the **walrus operator** `:=` to read up to 1 MB, assign it to `chunk`, and loop while it is non-empty. At end of file `read` returns `b""`, which is falsy.

`create_app` is an **app factory**: it builds and returns a new FastAPI app. Tests call it with their own `pipeline` (for example one with `HashingEmbedder`) and `corpus_dir`.
Creates the FastAPI app; the title and version appear in the generated OpenAPI docs at `/docs`.

A small mutable dict holds the pipeline. The nested functions below can change `state["pipeline"]` without the `nonlocal` keyword because they modify the dict, not rebind a variable. Line 60 is blank.
`get` returns the pipeline, creating it on first use.

If there is no pipeline yet, builds one. Re-ranking and translation are **on** by default here (`RAG_RERANK` and `RAG_TRANSLATE` default to `"1"`), because the evaluation shows that is the best configuration; set either to `0` to turn it off for speed.

The handler is `async` because it awaits file reads.
Checks the admin key first, before reading any upload, so unauthorised requests cost almost nothing.
Rejects more than `MAX_FILES` files (default 5) with HTTP 413.
Checks every file's extension before reading any of them, and rejects unsupported types with HTTP 415 (unsupported media type). `f.filename or ""` guards against a missing file name.
The comment states the rule: parse everything first, so one bad file leaves the index untouched. `parsed` maps file name to pages.
